name: Anne Beaufour
current_role: Board member of Ipsen (representing family holding Highrock S.à r.l.); director of family holding Mayroy
profile: Granddaughter of Dr. Henri Beaufour, founder of the labs that became French pharma group Ipsen. After her father Albert died in 2000 she and brother Henri controlled ~52-57% of Ipsen via Luxembourg holdings (Mayroy, Highrock, Beech Tree). Switzerland-based; Henri died in Nov 2025, his stake passing to a foundation.
interesting_fact: Ipsen traces back to the Beaufour laboratories founded in 1929 by her grandfather; she holds a geology degree from the University of Paris-Sud (Orsay).
notes: Extremely private; declines comment via Ipsen spokesperson. Brother Henri Beaufour died 28 Nov 2025 - avoid as an outreach topic. Best route is Ipsen corporate communications.

name: Mikheil Lomtadze
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board, Kaspi.kz
profile: Georgian-born Harvard MBA who joined Kaspi via private equity firm Baring Vostok, which invested in the Kazakh bank in 2006. As CEO he rebranded it Kaspi in 2011 and turned it into a super-app combining payments, marketplace and fintech; Kaspi listed in London (2020) and on Nasdaq (2024).
interesting_fact: Before Kaspi he was a partner at Baring Vostok, Russia's largest private equity fund; Kaspi's leadership team pointedly contained no career bankers when it pivoted to technology.
deep_cut_fact: While still a student in Tbilisi he founded his own audit and consulting firm, Georgia Consulting Group Audit (1995), which he later sold.

public_contacts.value: Fintech Leaders interview (Miguel Armaza) - prior podcast appearance

notes: Also spelled Mikhail Lomtadze. Does occasional long-form interviews (McKinsey, Fintech Leaders) - podcast-friendly. Best route: Kaspi IR.

name: Alfred Lerner
profile: Deceased: Alfred Lerner (1933-2002), chairman of credit card giant MBNA and owner of the Cleveland Browns (1998-2002), died October 23, 2002 in Cleveland. Matches the 1996-2000 Forbes listing.
notes: Died 2002 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Lerner ; NYT obituary https://www.nytimes.com/2002/10/25/sports/alfred-lerner-69-banker-revived-cleveland-browns.html). Identity inferred from Forbes 1996-2000 US listing at ~$3.8B; no source_of_wealth given in input. Son Randy Lerner inherited the Browns.

name: Zhou Jianping
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (via Hailan Group), HLA Group Corp. (Shanghai 600398); son Zhou Lichen is chairman
profile: Founder of HLA Group (Heilan Home), one of China's largest menswear makers and retailers. Starting from a small-town photo studio, he took over a collective wool mill in Xinqiao, Jiangyin in 1988 and launched the HLA retail brand around 2002 on a self-service, Uniqlo-style model; he has since handed the chairmanship to his son.
interesting_fact: He never attended university; the money for his first wool-mill venture came from running a photo studio.
deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he opened the first photo studio in his hometown of Xinqiao, Jiangyin; it sat opposite a wool mill, which is how he learned the textile trade before taking over the town's collective mill for 300,000 yuan in 1988.
notes: Very low profile; communicates via HLA's board secretary (Tang Yong). No published personal contact found; route via HLA Group investor relations / SSE roadshow platform.
